credit_headline.narrative: System-level bank credit growth eased slightly in August 2026, with non-food credit slipping to 18.8% from July's 19.1% — pausing a climb that had run from 15.8% in April — but still sitting near the top of its 26-period range. Underneath that, breadth stayed intact: all four main sectors have now posted positive growth for 26 straight periods, the longest such run on record, so the slight cooling at the headline level has not come with any sector dropping out of growth.

sibc-bank-credit-abs.title: Bank credit hits a record ₹223.9L Cr, up ₹3.1L Cr
sibc-bank-credit-abs.observation: Bank credit outstanding reached ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, the highest level in this 44-period series.
sibc-bank-credit-abs.direction: Volume rose ₹3.1L Cr period-on-period (₹220.8L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr), more than July's ₹1.5L Cr addition.
chain: Bank credit outstanding hit ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, up from ₹220.8L Cr in July — the highest level in this 44-period series.
The ₹3.1L Cr monthly addition is roughly double July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, on a book that has grown from ₹133.4L Cr in January 2023.
Bank credit has added ₹90.5L Cr since January 2023 (₹133.4L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr).
sibc-bank-credit-abs.inference: The ₹3.1L Cr monthly addition is roughly double July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, the strongest single-month build in at least the last two periods, keeping the book at an all-time high of ₹223.9L Cr.

sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.title: Bank credit FY26 growth hits 16.1%, up 5.1 points from FY25
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.observation: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year to March 2025 and 16.1% in the year to March 2026.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.direction: The full-year growth rate stepped up 5.1 points, from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26.
chain: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26.
That is a 5.1-point step-up between the two full years — a measure that moves only once a year, at each March close.
FY26's 16.1% is the faster of the two years by a clear margin.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.inference: A 5.1-point jump between full years is a large move for an annual growth measure that updates only once a year, marking a year-over-year step-up in FY26 lending versus FY25.

sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.title: Banks deployed a record ₹29.6L Cr net new credit in FY26
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.observation: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new credit in the full year to March 2026.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.direction: This figure is unchanged at ₹29.6L Cr since it was locked at the March 2026 year-end, and sits at or near the maximum of this 44-period series.
chain: FY26 net new credit stands at ₹29.6L Cr, at or near the maximum reading in this 44-period series.
The figure has not moved from ₹29.6L Cr across all 44 periods because it reflects the full-year tally fixed at the March 2026 close, not a monthly flow.
It won't update again until the FY27 year-end close.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.inference: Because this is a once-a-year figure fixed at the March close, its unchanged ₹29.6L Cr reading across 44 periods doesn't move with current conditions — the FY acceleration and monthly absolute signals carry that part of the story.

sibc-bank-credit-yoy.title: Bank credit growth eases to 19.08% from July's 19.33% peak
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.observation: Bank credit grew 19.08% year-on-year in August 2026, down from July's 19.33%.
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.direction: Growth slowed 0.25 points (19.33% → 19.08%), after rising every month from April's 16.0% through July's 19.3%.
chain: Bank credit grew 19.08% year-on-year in August 2026, slightly below July's 19.33%, the high point of this 26-period window.
The rate had climbed every month from April's 16.0% to July's 19.3%, before easing 0.25 points in August.
Even after the dip, August's 19.08% is still near the highest level in this 26-period window.
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.inference: August's slight pullback from July's 19.33% peak is the first deceleration after three straight months of increases (16.0% in April to 19.3% in July), though at 19.08% growth remains near the highest level recorded in this window.

sibc-food-credit-abs.title: Food credit falls to ₹1.12L Cr, a third straight decline
sibc-food-credit-abs.observation: Food credit outstanding fell to ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down ₹0.06L Cr from July's ₹1.18L Cr.
sibc-food-credit-abs.direction: Volume declined ₹0.06L Cr period-on-period (₹1.18L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), the third consecutive monthly drop since May's all-time high of ₹1.37L Cr.
chain: Food credit stood at ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down from ₹1.18L Cr in July.
This is the third straight monthly decline since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026, following drops to ₹1.32L Cr in June and ₹1.18L Cr in July.
Despite three months of decline, ₹1.12L Cr remains above the upper range of this 44-period window.
sibc-food-credit-abs.inference: Three consecutive monthly declines from May's ₹1.37L Cr peak have pulled food credit down by ₹0.25L Cr (₹1.37L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), yet the book is still reading in the upper range of this window — the pullback has not erased the earlier run-up.

sibc-food-credit-yoy.title: Food credit YoY growth jumps to 145.81%, a series high
sibc-food-credit-yoy.observation: Food credit grew 145.81% year-on-year in August 2026, the highest reading in this 32-period series.
sibc-food-credit-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated 37.90 points (107.91% → 145.81%), surpassing the prior high of 139.4% set in March 2026.
chain: Food credit grew 145.81% year-on-year in August 2026, up from 107.91% in July — a 37.90-point jump.
This surpasses the previous high of 139.4% reached in March 2026, making August the strongest reading in this 32-period series.
At 145.81%, growth is now well above the lower end of this window's range (23.0%).
sibc-food-credit-yoy.inference: The 37.90-point jump to 145.81% is the largest year-on-year growth figure in this 32-period series, well clear of the prior high of 139.4% set in March 2026.

sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.title: Non-food credit hits a record ₹222.8L Cr, up ₹3.2L Cr
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.observation: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, the highest level in this 44-period series.
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.direction: Volume rose ₹3.2L Cr period-on-period (₹219.6L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr), continuing the climb from ₹132.9L Cr in January 2023.
chain: Non-food credit stood at ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, up from ₹219.6L Cr in July — the highest level in this 44-period series.
The ₹3.2L Cr monthly addition builds on a run that has taken the book from ₹132.9L Cr in January 2023 to today's level.
Non-food credit has added ₹89.9L Cr since January 2023 (₹132.9L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr).
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.inference: Non-food credit's ₹3.2L Cr addition in August keeps the book at a fresh all-time high of ₹222.8L Cr, extending a climb that has added ₹89.9L Cr since January 2023.

sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.title: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr net new non-food credit in FY26
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.observation: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr of net new non-food credit in the year to March 2026.
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.direction: This figure is unchanged at ₹29.2L Cr since the March 2026 year-end close, and sits at or near the maximum for this 44-period series.
chain: FY26 non-food credit addition stands at ₹29.2L Cr, at or near the maximum reading in this 44-period series.
It has not moved from ₹29.2L Cr across all 44 periods, since this is the full-year figure locked at the March 2026 close, not a monthly flow.
This figure is fixed until the March 2027 close.
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.inference: This FY26 figure is fixed until the next annual lock in March 2027, so it won't reflect any shift until then — the monthly absolute reading is what moves in between.

sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.title: Non-food credit eases to 18.8%, still near 26-period high
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.observation: Non-food credit grew 18.8% year-on-year in August 2026.
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.direction: Growth slipped from 19.1% in July to 18.8% in August, down 0.29 points.
chain: Non-food credit grew 18.8% year-on-year in August 2026, down from July's 19.1%.
This ends a three-month climb that ran from 15.8% in April to 19.1% in July.
Even after the dip, 18.8% sits above the upper range of this 26-period window (where most readings fall between 10.5% and 14.8%).
The slowdown is small next to the run-up that preceded it — a 0.29-point easing after a near four-point climb since April.
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.inference: This is the first easing after three straight months of acceleration, but at 18.8% growth is still running well above every level seen in this dataset outside the last few months.

sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.title: All 4 main sectors stay positive — 26th straight period
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.observation: All four main sectors — agriculture, industry, services, retail — posted positive year-on-year growth in August 2026.
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.direction: Breadth held at 4 of 4 sectors, unchanged from July, extending a run that began in July 2024.
chain: All four main sectors show positive YoY growth in August 2026, with breadth unchanged at 4 of 4 from July.
This is the 26th consecutive period at 4 of 4, a streak that has held since Jul 2024.
Against a historical record of 38 periods, the current reading sits at or near the maximum for that window.
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.inference: At 26 straight periods, this is the longest stretch in the dataset where every main sector has grown together, against a record that includes a stretch in 2023 when none did.

sector_mix.narrative: Trade credit growth stays split between the two sub-sectors: Wholesale Trade at 26.2% year-on-year against Retail Trade's 13.0%. The 13.2-point gap between them has widened from 12.7 points last period, as Wholesale's growth picked up further while Retail held steady — undoing the narrowing seen in the prior reading.

sibc-agriculture-share.title: Agriculture's share falls to 12.23%, tying its 2023 low
sibc-agriculture-share.observation: Agriculture's share of total bank credit fell to 12.23% in Aug 2026.
sibc-agriculture-share.direction: Share slipped 0.09pp from 12.33% in Jul 2026 to 12.23%, falling below the 25th percentile of 12.4% across 44 periods.
chain: Agriculture's share dropped to 12.23% in Aug 2026, down 0.09pp from 12.33% in Jul 2026.
The reading sits below the 25th percentile of 12.4% across 44 periods, in the lower range of its history.
The series has only touched this level once before, at 12.2% in Nov 2023.
sibc-agriculture-share.inference: At 12.23%, agriculture's share matches its lowest point since Nov 2023 — a repeat low rather than a new one, even as the sector's own credit growth is strengthening.

sibc-agriculture-yoy.title: Agriculture credit growth rises to 17.22% YoY, up 0.25pp
sibc-agriculture-yoy.observation: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026.
sibc-agriculture-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated 0.25pp from 16.98% in Jul 2026 to 17.22%.
chain: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.25pp from 16.98% in Jul 2026.
This sits near the median of its 32-period range, between the 25th percentile of 9.5% and the 75th percentile of 17.4%.
The series ran at 20.0% for three straight months in Jan-Mar 2024, well above today's 17.22%.
sibc-agriculture-yoy.inference: Agriculture's growth has reaccelerated to 17.22%, but that is still a middling reading for this sector — the series held at 20.0% for three straight months in early 2024, a level the current reading hasn't reached.

sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.title: Industry FY credit growth jumps to 15.0% from 8.2%
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.observation: Industry credit grew 15.0% in the year to Mar 2026, up from 8.2% in the year to Mar 2025.
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.direction: Full-year growth stepped up 6.8 points, from 8.2% in FY25 to 15.0% in FY26.
chain: Industry credit grew 8.2% in the year to Mar 2025 and 15.0% in the year to Mar 2026.
That is a 6.8-point step-up in annual growth, set once at the Mar 2026 year-end.
FY26's 15.0% rate is nearly double FY25's 8.2%.
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.inference: This is an annual measure, fixed only at the Mar 2026 year-end: industry credit's annual growth nearly doubled between FY25 and FY26, from 8.2% to 15.0%.

sibc-industry-share.title: Industry's share drops to 21.53%, matching its 2026 low
sibc-industry-share.observation: Industry's share of total bank credit stood at 21.53% in Aug 2026.
sibc-industry-share.direction: Share fell 0.33pp from 21.86% in Jul 2026 to 21.53%, below the 25th percentile of 21.7%.
chain: Industry's share fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026, down 0.33pp from 21.86% in Jul 2026.
The reading is below the 25th percentile of 21.7% across 44 periods, in the lower range of its history.
The series already touched 21.5% four times in 2026 — Jan, Feb, Mar and Apr.
sibc-industry-share.inference: Industry's 21.53% share matches the 21.5% floor already seen four times in 2026, making Aug a repeat low rather than a new one.

sibc-industry-yoy.title: Industry credit growth slows to 18.23% YoY after 20% peak
sibc-industry-yoy.observation: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026.
sibc-industry-yoy.direction: Growth decelerated 1.72pp from 19.95% in Jul 2026 to 18.23% — the first pullback since the climb from May 2025's 5.3% low.
chain: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026, down 1.72pp from 19.95% in Jul 2026.
That follows a climb from a 5.3% low in May 2025 to a 20.0% peak in Jul 2026.
Even after the pullback, 18.23% stays above the 75th percentile of 13.9% across this 26-period window.
sibc-industry-yoy.inference: This is industry credit's first deceleration since the run from a 5.3% low in May 2025 to a 20.0% peak in Jul 2026 — the pullback to 18.23% stays above the 75th percentile of 13.9%, reading as a pause near the highs rather than a reversal.

sibc-infra-yoy.title: Infrastructure credit growth holds at 10.18% YoY
sibc-infra-yoy.observation: Infrastructure credit grew 10.18% YoY in Aug 2026.
sibc-infra-yoy.direction: Growth was flat, down just 0.04pp from 10.23% in Jul 2026 to 10.18%, just under May 2026's 11.6% peak.
chain: Infrastructure credit grew 10.18% YoY in Aug 2026, almost unchanged from 10.23% in Jul 2026.
That keeps growth above the 75th percentile of 8.6% across 32 periods, in the upper range of its history.
It remains below the series peak of 11.6% hit in May 2026, after a -1.3% contraction in May 2025.
sibc-infra-yoy.inference: Infrastructure credit growth has plateaued just under its 11.6% May 2026 peak, holding above the 75th percentile of 8.6% — a sharp turnaround from the -1.3% contraction recorded in May 2025.

sibc-main-acceleration.title: Services leads acceleration at +1.40pp; Industry reverses -1.72pp
sibc-main-acceleration.observation: Services accelerated 1.40pp, the fastest of the four main sectors in this scan, while Industry decelerated 1.72pp, the only one to slow.
sibc-main-acceleration.direction: The spread between the fastest (Services, +1.40pp) and slowest (Industry, -1.72pp) widened to 3.12pp.
chain: Services accelerated 1.40pp, Personal Loans 0.69pp, and Agriculture 0.25pp, while Industry decelerated 1.72pp.
That is a 3.12pp spread between the fastest and slowest mover, with Industry flipping from strengthening to weakening status.
Personal Loans moved the other way, shifting from stable to strengthening status.
sibc-main-acceleration.inference: Industry is the only one of the four main sectors reversing direction, dropping from strengthening to weakening (-1.72pp) just as Personal Loans flips from stable to strengthening (+0.69pp) — the -0.29pp rotation mass shows the overall mix barely moved even as individual sectors swapped places.

sibc-main-allocation.title: New-credit allocation: Services and Personal Loans swing widest
sibc-main-allocation.observation: Across the readings in this scan, Personal Loans' share of new 12-month credit ranged 30.0%-33.2%, Services 27.0%-36.0%, Industry 21.0%-21.6%, and Agriculture 11.4%-12.4%, with the group together capturing 94.7% of total allocation.
sibc-main-allocation.direction: Industry and Agriculture held in tight bands (21.0%-21.6% and 11.4%-12.4%), while Services and Personal Loans swung far wider (27.0%-36.0% and 30.0%-33.2%).
chain: Services' allocation share ranged from 27.0% to 36.0% and Personal Loans from 30.0% to 33.2% across this scan, the two widest bands of the four main sectors.
Industry held a tight 21.0%-21.6% band and Agriculture 11.4%-12.4%, the two narrowest.
The spread between the top and bottom readings is 83.4%, and the rotation mass — the share of the mix that moved — is 35.98pp.
sibc-main-allocation.inference: Services and Personal Loans show far more movement in their share of new credit (9.0-point and 3.2-point bands) than Industry and Agriculture (0.6-point and 1.0-point bands), consistent with a 35.98pp rotation mass across the mix.

sibc-main-momentum.title: Services adds ₹12.3L Cr over 12 months, all sectors strengthening
sibc-main-momentum.observation: Services added ₹12.3L Cr of bank credit over the last 12 months, the most of the four main sectors.
sibc-main-momentum.direction: Personal Loans added ₹10.5L Cr, Industry ₹7.4L Cr and Agriculture ₹4.0L Cr — a spread of ₹8.3L Cr between Services and Agriculture, with all four sectors in strengthening status.
chain: Services added ₹12.3L Cr of bank credit over the last 12 months, ahead of Personal Loans at ₹10.5L Cr, Industry at ₹7.4L Cr and Agriculture at ₹4.0L Cr.
All four main sectors are marked strengthening, so none is losing momentum even as the amounts added differ widely.
The gap between the top and bottom sector is ₹8.3L Cr, with Services and Personal Loans together adding ₹22.8L Cr against Industry and Agriculture's combined ₹11.4L Cr.
sibc-main-momentum.inference: Services and Personal Loans continue to account for the bulk of new bank credit deployment among the four main sectors, even with all four still marked strengthening.

sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.title: Personal Loans hold 32.6% of bank credit, Industry slips to 21.4%
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.observation: Personal Loans account for 32.6% of all bank credit, the largest of the four main sectors, while Agriculture holds the smallest share at 12.2%.
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.direction: Personal Loans and Services are gaining share (32.6% and 28.1%), while Industry (21.4%) and Agriculture (12.2%) are losing it, a gap of 20.4 points between the top and bottom sector.
chain: Personal Loans hold 32.6% of all bank credit and Services 28.1%, together 60.7% of the four main sectors, while Industry holds 21.4% and Agriculture 12.2%.
Personal Loans and Services are both marked strengthening in their share, while Industry and Agriculture are both weakening.
The 20.4 point gap between Personal Loans and Agriculture is the full spread across the four main sectors.
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.inference: Personal Loans and Services are gaining share of overall bank credit at the same time Industry and Agriculture are losing it, with a 20.4 point gap now separating the top and bottom sector.

sibc-main-share-scan.title: Services swings to strengthening at 28.3% share of non-food credit
sibc-main-share-scan.observation: Services holds 28.3% of non-food credit and has shifted from weakening to strengthening, while Personal Loans leads at 32.7%.
sibc-main-share-scan.direction: Personal Loans holds the largest share at 32.7%, ahead of Services at 28.3%, Industry at 21.5% and Agriculture at 12.2% — a spread of 20.5 points between the top and bottom sector.
chain: Services' share of non-food credit stands at 28.3%, and its status has flipped from weakening to strengthening this period.
Personal Loans still leads the mix at 32.7%, with Industry at 21.5% and Agriculture at 12.2% both still marked weakening.
Services is now the only one of the four sectors to have changed direction, moving from losing share to gaining it.
sibc-main-share-scan.inference: Services is the one main sector whose share of non-food credit has turned from weakening to strengthening this period, while Personal Loans keeps the largest share at 32.7% and Industry and Agriculture continue to lose ground.

sibc-main-size-scan.title: Main sector bank credit at ₹211.1L Cr, highest in this 44-month series
sibc-main-size-scan.observation: Bank credit to the four main sectors reached ₹211.1L Cr in Aug 2026, the highest level in this 44-period series.
sibc-main-size-scan.direction: The total rose from ₹208.9L Cr last period to ₹211.1L Cr, up ₹2.2L Cr, and is up from ₹126.4L Cr in Jan 2023.
chain: Main-sector bank credit stands at ₹211.1L Cr in Aug 2026, up ₹2.2L Cr from ₹208.9L Cr the prior period.
That is the highest reading in the full 44-period series, which began at ₹126.4L Cr in Jan 2023.
The total has grown ₹84.7L Cr since Jan 2023 (₹126.4L Cr → ₹211.1L Cr), with the current reading at the top of that range.
sibc-main-size-scan.inference: At ₹211.1L Cr, main-sector bank credit is at its highest point across the full 44-period series that started at ₹126.4L Cr in Jan 2023.

sibc-main-yoy-scan.title: Services leads main sectors at 24.3%, spread widens to 7.4%
sibc-main-yoy-scan.observation: Services grew 24.3% YoY, the fastest of the four main sectors, ahead of Industry at 18.2%, Agriculture and Allied Activities at 17.2%, and Personal Loans at 16.9%.
sibc-main-yoy-scan.direction: Services' YoY rose 22.9% → 24.3% while Industry eased 20.0% → 18.2%, widening the spread between fastest and slowest to 7.4% from 6.7%.
chain: Services grew 24.3% YoY, up from 22.9% last period and the fastest of the four main sectors.
Industry's growth eased to 18.2% from 20.0%, a slowdown, while Agriculture (17.2%, up from 17.0%) and Personal Loans (16.9%, up from 16.2%) both ticked up.
The spread between the fastest (Services) and slowest (Personal Loans) widened to 7.4% from 6.7%, and Industry's status shifted from strengthening to active.
Services is pulling further ahead of the other three main sectors, while Industry is the only one of the four losing pace.
sibc-main-yoy-scan.inference: Services, at 24.3% YoY, is the only main sector still gaining pace from an already-leading level, while Industry is the sole sector slowing this period, down to 18.2% from 20.0% even as it remains the second-fastest of the four.

sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.title: NBFC credit: PFIs accelerate 4.26 points, HFCs decelerate 1.07 points
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.observation: Public Financial Institutions' YoY growth rate rose 4.26 points this period, while Housing Finance Companies' rate fell 1.07 points.
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.direction: PFIs accelerated by 4.26 points while HFCs decelerated by 1.07 points, flipping HFCs from strengthening to weakening.
chain: PFIs' YoY growth rate rose 4.26 points this period, the strengthening side of NBFC credit's two parts.
HFCs' rate fell 1.07 points, reversing its status from strengthening to weakening.
The gap between the two moves is 5.33 points, with 1.82 points of the mix having rotated between them.
PFIs are the sole source of acceleration in NBFC credit's two components this period, with HFCs now pulling the other way.
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.inference: PFIs' 4.26-point acceleration stands against HFCs' 1.07-point slowdown, and HFCs' flip to weakening is the only status change across NBFC credit's two parts this period.

sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.title: NBFC credit allocation: PFIs up to 72.5%, HFCs down to 10.8%
sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.observation: Public Financial Institutions took as much as 72.5% of new NBFC credit in one reading in this distribution, while Housing Finance Companies took as little as 10.8% in another.
sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.direction: Across the nine readings, Public Financial Institutions' share ranged as high as 72.5% and as low as 12.7%, while Housing Finance Companies ranged from 27.5% down to 10.8%, with the combined total at 34.6% in one reading.
chain: Public Financial Institutions' share of new NBFC credit reached 72.5% in the top reading of this 9-entity distribution, with other PFI readings at 28.3%, 17.0%, and 12.7%.
Housing Finance Companies' readings ran 27.5%, 20.2%, 17.7%, and as low as 10.8%.
The spread between the highest (72.5%) and lowest (10.8%) readings is 61.7 points, with 72.47 points of the mix in rotation.

sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.inference: Public Financial Institutions' top reading of 72.5% of new NBFC credit allocation is more than double Housing Finance Companies' highest reading of 27.5%, showing a wider and higher-reaching set of allocation values for Public Financial Institutions across these nine cuts.

sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.title: NBFC credit: PFIs add 1.67 lakh units, HFCs just 63,524
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.observation: Public Financial Institutions added 1.67 lakh units of NBFC credit over the trailing 12 months, against 63,524 for Housing Finance Companies.
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.direction: PFIs' 12-month addition of 1.67 lakh units is 1.04 lakh higher than HFCs' 63,524, the full spread between NBFC credit's two parts.
chain: Public Financial Institutions added 1.67 lakh units of NBFC credit over the trailing 12 months, versus 63,524 for Housing Finance Companies.
The gap between the two, 1.04 lakh units, is the full spread in this 2-entity distribution.
PFIs' addition is 1.04 lakh units higher than HFCs', concentrating most of the 12-month build in one part of NBFC credit.
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.inference: Public Financial Institutions added 1.67 lakh units of NBFC credit against Housing Finance Companies' 63,524 over the same 12 months, making Public Financial Institutions the larger of the two contributors to NBFC credit's 12-month build-up.

sibc-nbfc-sub-share-scan.title: NBFC share gap narrows to 0.7 points as PFIs close in
sibc-nbfc-sub-share-scan.observation: Housing Finance Companies hold 17.7% of NBFC credit against Public Financial Institutions' 17.0%, a spread of 0.7 points.
sibc-nbfc-sub-share-scan.direction: The gap has narrowed sharply from 1.2 points last period (HFCs 18.0%, PFIs 16.7%) to 0.7 points now (HFCs 17.7%, PFIs 17.0%).

sibc-services-acceleration.title: Aviation's YoY growth jumps 8.28 points, fastest in services

psl.narrative: Priority sector lending is splitting into two speeds. Export Credit (-9.7%) and Others (-3.3%) remain in decline, widening the gap between the fastest and slowest PSL sub-category from 45.6 to 51.2.

sibc-psl-acceleration.title: Social Infrastructure leads PSL acceleration, +4.74 points

sibc-psl-acceleration.inference: Three segments reversed direction in a single period — Export Credit, Others and Renewable Energy all went from strengthening to weakening — while Social Infrastructure and Micro and Small Enterprises made the opposite switch, pointing to momentum rotating across segments rather than building in one direction.

sibc-psl-agri-yoy.title: PSL Agriculture holds at 19.44% YoY, above its upper range

sibc-psl-education-yoy.title: PSL Educational Loans ease to 15.91% YoY, down 0.80 points

sibc-psl-housing-yoy.title: PSL Housing growth falls to 9.55% YoY, a third straight drop

sibc-psl-medium-yoy.title: PSL Medium Enterprises hit a new high at 31.01% YoY

sibc-psl-others-yoy.title: PSL Others reverses to -3.35% YoY, ending 4-period improvement streak

sibc-psl-renewable-yoy.title: PSL Renewable Energy growth cools to 25.96%, down 5.74 points
